title: Grant Tracker for Wealth management Firm Owners
oneLiner: A workflow engine that handles grant & funding tracking end to end and hands a human the exceptions rather than the queue. Aimed at wealth management firm owners, built for one person, not a department.
problem: Wealth management teams lose reporting deadlines discovered the week they are due. A typical wealth management operation runs this on people, memory, and a shared spreadsheet. The cost is invisible on any P&L line, which is why it never gets fixed.
solution: A workflow engine that handles grant & funding tracking end to end and hands a human the exceptions rather than the queue. Revenue is data subscription, which suits a buyer who wants the cost to track the value rather than the seat count.
scoreRationale: Carried by feasibility (92), held back by timing (31).

build.hardestPart: The data you need lives on paper in a back office; digitisation is half the product.

whyNow: Connectors exist for systems that were closed five years ago. Wealth management is growing at roughly 14% a year, and this job has not been re-tooled since it was designed around paper.

title: Wealth management Intake Triage on Voice
oneLiner: A voice agent that handles intake & triage end to end and hands a human the exceptions rather than the queue. Aimed at wealth management firm owners, finding what the inspector would find, first.
problem: Wealth management teams lose the front-desk queue that swallows 11 hours a week. Every wealth management team solves this the same way: someone stays late. It scales linearly with headcount, so growth makes it worse rather than better.
solution: A narrow voice agent scoped to intake & triage alone — no platform, no migration, no six-month rollout. Revenue is per-outcome, which suits a buyer who wants the cost to track the value rather than the seat count.
scoreRationale: Carried by money (87), held back by competition (39).

build.hardestPart: Trust has to be earned before anyone lets this run unsupervised.

whyNow: Real-time speech models fell below $0.06 a minute in 2025. Wealth management is growing at roughly 14% a year, and this job has not been re-tooled since it was designed around paper.
